page: Amazon Web Services c9g.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It is powered by 32 dedicated physical cores across an arm64 AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 processor operating at 3.3 GHz. Each core runs a single thread, eliminating hyperthreading contention. The hardware features 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 64.0 GB, providing 2.0 GB per vCPU in a typical 1:2 compute-focused ratio. The instance includes 17 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, operates with no local storage disks attached, and contains no graphical accelerators.

Benchmark measurements show strong multi-threaded and memory-bound throughput. In Geekbench testing, the server scores 2,382 in single-core and 25,987 in multi-core metrics, achieving top-tier ranking in compilation tests using Clang (63,901.0) and text processing (3,123.0). Memory evaluations via PassMark place its memory score in the top 10 percent (4,502.98), mirrored by high-throughput database operations (47,005.39) and strong Redis SET throughput reaching 93.19 million operations per second. Data processing tasks show high efficiency, yielding top-tier single-threaded gzip compression at 36.46 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 17.26 GB/sec.

Hardware tradeoffs center around the compute-optimized architecture and the absence of integrated resources. Because local storage is absent, all persistent storage operations rely entirely on remote network-attached volumes, making standard I/O dependent on overall network utilization. In addition, the 2.0 GB per core memory footprint restricts this instance from hosting monolithic in-memory databases requiring large working footprints, despite high cached memory bandwidth. The absence of AVX and AMX instruction extensions shifts high-performance vector processing strictly onto ARM-native operations.

Workload fit is best aligned with compute-intensive batch jobs, continuous integration and software compilation pipelines, microservices, and static web serving, where it registered 92.57 GB/sec throughput. Its balanced compute footprint also supports non-GPU CPU inference workflows for small-to-medium models, such as 7B parameter models generating 27.58 tokens per second.
description: Amazon Web Services c9g.8xlarge is a compute-optimized arm64 instance powered by a 32-core AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 processor running at 3.3 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor. Configured with a dedicated core-per-vCPU topology, it offers 64.0 GB of system memory, matching a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The server provides 17 Gbps of baseline networking capacity, contains zero GPUs, and includes no local NVMe storage, relying entirely on network-attached storage. Benchmark testing shows top-tier Clang software compilation throughput (63,901.0) and high Geekbench multi-core efficiency (25,987.0), supported by solid multi-core stress-ng scores. Data-handling metrics demonstrate high throughput in PassMark database operations and static web serving (92.57 GB/sec). With its balance of core density and dedicated execution threads, c9g.8xlarge is suited for software build pipelines, distributed compute tasks, web serving fleets, and CPU-based lightweight machine learning inference.
